meta.source_system: event-driven teaching fragment: a close handshake with event-labeled edges (hand-constructed minimal example for this repository, not transcribed from a real system; shaped after the lesson of an external RFC 9293 spot-check)
meta.encoding: states 0/1/2/4 = open / wait-fin / closing / time-wait; states 3, 5, 6, 7 = unreachable padding (power-of-two input contract, same rule as the 512 / 16,384-state real cases): every event self-loops, reward 0
meta.semantics_class: event: the four actions are external events named by the protocol; their names are part of the behavior and do not follow state renamings -> declare semantics "fixed" (docs/judge-semantics.md)
meta.transcription_rules: fragment merges the normal-close wait states into one state 1 and the simultaneous-close branch into state 2; rcv FIN while open enters state 2 (both FINs then outstanding); rcv RST tears down to the terminal state 4 with a penalty; repeating an event whose precondition is gone is an illegal self-loop at -1
meta.reward_rule: +1 when the close completes (the state's own completion event arrives); -1 for illegal attempts and resets; 0 in the terminal state and padding
meta.structural_fact: states 1 and 2 are structurally identical (one outgoing edge into the goal each, otherwise only penalized self-loops) but their completion events differ: rcv FIN vs rcv ACK of FIN
